h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to identify which settings are strong, weak or neutral, and which parts can be cut off from the outcome by other settings. Build hypotheses mainly from (a) the edited field's current value in the parent, since replacing a strong value with a weak one hurts and filling an empty or harmful slot helps, and (b) conditions that disconnect the edited part, which shrink its effect. When finding flaws, replace any hypothesis whose direction could plausibly reverse because of a competing effect, or whose mechanism relies on partial redundancy between different parts. Ensure varied edit fields and values. State a one-sentence mechanism.

hyps.why: Filling an empty first-hop slot with a strong conv restores the whole node-1 path, a larger gain than replacing any existing op.
Filling an empty edge with a strong conv adds capacity, more than upgrading an existing op.
Adding a conv to an empty edge into the output node gives a large gain.
A conv on a previously empty edge into the output adds a trainable path and gives a large gain.
Filling the empty direct edge with a conv adds a strong input-to-output path.
Deleting a strong conv into the output loses much more than deleting a weak op, which has little to lose.
Removing a strong conv from the first hop cuts the main feature path, which hurts more than removing a weak op.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 gets no input, so edge 2 is dead and its edit has almost no effect.
Edge 4 reads from the disconnected node 1, so the conv adds nothing when edge 0 is none.
A skip from a dead node 1 carries no signal, so its usual benefit disappears.
